chat: use Agent Host defaults across chat entry points

Use shared harness selection for new chat conversations.

- Enable the Copilot harness preference without experiment control.
- Use default-aware routing for Quick Chat, inline handoff, model offers, and voice.
- Keep explicit harness choices and managed policy precedence.
- Remove the Agent Sessions welcome page and its unused support code.
- Add tests for routing, input state, model selection, and session lifetime.

Follow-up to #345901.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed branch, unique-resource generation, clear/reinitialize call path, and cache ownership are directly traced. `ChatSessionsService` caches every synthetic untitled session in `_sessions`; that synthetic object has `onWillDispose: Event.None`, and model-reference teardown has no call to `_disposeSession`. The only uncertainty is typical user reset count, which affects magnitude rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UUID-keyed `ContributedChatSessionData`, synthetic `IChatSession`, URI, option-map, and listener objects retained in `ChatSessionsService._sessions`
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One unreachable cache entry is retained per Quick Chat clear/new-draft operation; cost grows linearly with abandoned drafts for the lifetime of the provider/workbench.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: unbounded retained memory and increasing GC/cleanup cost over the workbench lifetime
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Quick Chat always called `startNewLocalSession`; disposing the model reference released an empty local session, as opposed to inserting a synthetic contributed session into `ChatSessionsService._sessions`.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Clearing Quick Chat now acquires a uniquely addressed contributed Agent Host draft. Disposing the prior `modelRef` removes the chat model, but the contributed-session cache entry created during acquisition is not removed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added non-local branch at `chatQuick.ts:444` replaces the previous `startNewLocalSession(...)`-only initialization with `acquireOrLoadSession(getNewChatSessionResource(...))`; `getNewChatSessionResource` generates a fresh UUID for every Agent Host draft, including every `clear()` replacement.
Findings.Title: Evict abandoned Agent Host drafts from the session cache
Findings.Impact: In a long-running window, repeatedly using Clear/New Chat in Quick Chat (and the same new default path used by voice drafts) grows the contributed-session cache linearly. The retained URIs, session wrappers, option maps, and listeners increase memory/GC pressure and make cache-wide provider cleanup progressively more expensive.
Findings.Evidence: `QuickChat.clear()` disposes `modelRef`, clears `modelPromise`, and immediately calls `initializeModel`; the added line then acquires a fresh Agent Host URI. `ChatSessionsService._getOrCreateChatSession` synthesizes untitled Agent Host sessions and stores each in `_sessions` as `ContributedChatSessionData`. Its removal callback only listens to `session.onWillDispose`, but synthetic sessions use `Event.None`; searches show `_disposeSession` is only reached from provider-item removal/deletion, not chat-model disposal. Therefore the UUID-keyed cache entry survives after Quick Chat releases the model.
Findings.Recommendation: Tie synthetic untitled contributed-session cache ownership to the corresponding chat-model lifetime (or add an explicit release API and invoke it when an untitled draft is abandoned), while preserving entries that are still referenced or have materialized aliases.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, submit, clear, and reopen Quick Chat under the new Copilot Agent Host default.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Quick Chat UI appears before initialization completes, but programmatic submission and normal submit handling await policy settlement, Agent Host draft acquisition, and host Ask-mode resolution. First send then materializes the draft before dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve an Agent Host draft and, on first send, create/materialize the host session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One contributed-session acquisition per initial Quick Chat model and per clear; one Agent Host session-creation/dispatch sequence on the first send. Repeated `whenReady` calls do not multiply acquisition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Quick Chat synchronously created an in-memory local session and did not enter the contributed-session cache or Agent Host materialization path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Draft acquisition and mode readiness gate submission; backend materialization gates first-send dispatch. The visible input itself is available while acquisition runs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of Quick Chat clear/new-draft operations over the lifetime of a workbench window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initialization is one promise per Quick Chat instance; overlapping query opens share it and only the latest query submits. Clearing starts one replacement acquisition. Distinct UUID drafts do not coalesce.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each Agent Host draft uses a fresh UUID, so acquisition is cold per new/cleared conversation. Repeated `whenReady` calls for the same Quick Chat are coalesced by `modelPromise`, and overlapping identical remote loads are coalesced by `ChatService._remoteSessionLoads`. Synthetic untitled sessions are cached in `ChatSessionsService._sessions` but are not evicted when the final chat-model reference is disposed, which is the reported regression.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: unique URI generation, cache insertion, absent disposal event, and model-reference teardown were all traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The retained object set per abandoned draft is small, and typical clear counts are unknown; retention is nevertheless unbounded over a long workbench lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: every abandoned unique Agent Host draft remains in the contributed-session cache after its model is released.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continue an inline chat request in the panel.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Handoff waits for account policy, destination acquisition, panel opening, selected-file attachment, and input acceptance before disposing inline chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the default Agent Host draft, open it in Chat, attach the selected range, and submit the prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destination session acquisition and one first-send materialization per handoff; one selected-file attachment at most in this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The handoff synchronously created a local chat model, opened it, and submitted without Agent Host draft/materialization work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All are awaited before handoff completes and the inline session is disposed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per user-initiated inline-to-panel handoff, independent of workspace file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One sequential chain per handoff. Session/editing-session disposal cancels acquisition; there is no per-file or per-selection fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A handoff creates one fresh destination draft. `acquireOrLoadSession` coalesces only matching resources; cancellation releases a late model reference. No repeated negative-cache retry is introduced within one handoff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed critical path and cancellation behavior; no scaling multiplicity was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold Agent Host and policy-settlement latency varies by environment, but operation count is fixed at one and required by the routing change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance finding: the new boundary is intentional one-per-handoff work, is awaited for required routing, and is cancellation-safe.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a voice target and send a first utterance, including floating-window operation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating a target waits for policy and draft acquisition, then awaits switching a host if present. First voice send waits through queued materialization so it can adopt the real session before completing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the default harness, materialize the untitled Agent Host session, send the utterance, and switch/adopt the returned resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One draft acquisition per New Session click; one Agent Host materialization/send per first utterance; at most one materialized-session load when the target is owned but not displayed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Voice New Session synchronously created a local model; direct fallback sends used that local resource and did not materialize an Agent Host session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creation and first-send materialization are on the voice action's critical path so the target can be switched and adopted consistently.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of voice New Session clicks and first utterances; no collection-sized multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-send queue results are awaited serially. Distinct New Session clicks are not UI-disabled or coalesced, though generation checks reject stale completions and dispose their model references.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Voice session creation uses a fresh untitled resource. Chat-service loads coalesce only identical resources; distinct rapid New Session clicks can overlap, but obsolete references are released. The shared synthetic-session cache retention is covered by the reported Quick Chat cache-lifecycle finding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for operation placement, generation handling, and lack of UI coalescing; no independent expensive fan-out beyond user click cardinality was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rapid-click prevalence and cold host duration are unknown; stale model references are released, limiting transient model retention.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the shared cache leak: required IPC is one per conversation, stale model references are cleaned up, and no high-confidence throughput regression was proven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and activate the Chat status-bar model promotion.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opportunity recomputation runs during status-entry updates; clicking Try waits for session restoration, policy settlement, and at most one session load before model selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load a new default-harness session before selecting a harness-specific promoted model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one session load per Try click when the current harness lacks the promoted model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Try switched to a local session when needed; it did not load a non-local default harness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The load is awaited before selecting the model; ordinary promo recomputation performs only in-memory scans.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered language models for in-memory scans; one boundary load per user click at most.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event-driven and serialized by the command invocation; no loop launches concurrent boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The status promo scans the current in-memory language-model registry and reads small storage sets. It has no new network cache or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: scans and single-load command flow were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Language-model registry size and configuration-event frequency vary, but both are small and user/configuration driven.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added scans are bounded and infrequent, and the only boundary is one intentional session load per activation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start VS Code with the retired Agent Sessions welcome-page setting and render session/welcome UI.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Startup no longer imports/registers or opens the retired Agent Sessions welcome editor. The standard Welcome page may open after migration according to existing startup behavior.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One startup editor per window; removed session list previously scaled with visible session results.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrent boundary work is introduced; deleted startup contribution work is removed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Startup configuration migration is a one-time setting migration. Removing the Agent Sessions welcome contribution removes its session-list/chat-widget allocations and does not add a cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for startup call-path removal and absence of new boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The relative render cost of the old and standard welcome pages was not measured, but the diff clearly removes rather than adds the retired surface's allocations and session loading.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the migration/removal reduces startup contribution and UI work. The removed result limiter was only used by the deleted welcome surface, so it does not uncap a surviving list.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a standard editor or view chat under the changed default preference.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: New editor/view chat resolution waits for policy and default-harness acquisition; first send materializes the draft. Existing chat editor/view code already implemented this path, while this PR changes its default reachability.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Route new chats through the Agent Host contributed-session and first-send materialization path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Agent Host draft acquisition and one first-send materialization per newly created default conversation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor-specific Copilot harness preference defaulted off, preserving local creation in scenarios where that preference controlled routing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Acquisition gates model readiness; first-send materialization gates dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of new conversations, not messages or workspace items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One acquisition per new conversation. ChatService coalesces duplicate loads by resource and cancels abandoned loads when consumer count reaches zero.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The setting default now selects Copilot Agent Host for ordinary new chats unless policy, availability, explicit choice, or remembered opt-out overrides it. Each fresh non-local draft is uniquely keyed; identical-resource loads coalesce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for routing and boundary placement; no multiplicative fan-out was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold-host latency and adoption prevalence vary; the work is one-per-conversation and is the intended product behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for intended one-per-conversation Agent Host work; caching/coalescing is present. The abandoned-draft cache lifecycle is reported on the newly changed Quick Chat path where repeated resets expose unbounded growth.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all changed files and relevant call paths. Found one introduced cache-lifecycle regression: uniquely keyed Agent Host drafts created by the new Quick Chat routing remain cached after model disposal. Session creation, inline handoff, voice materialization, promo routing, startup migration, list changes, cold/warm behavior, and effective concurrency were otherwise bounded or intentional.
